query_vector.definition: For each token position, attention constructs a query vector: a numeric representation of what that position needs to find in the surrounding sequence.

key_vector.definition: Each position also produces a key vector.

value_vector.definition: Each position produces a value vector through another learned projection.

information_bottleneck.definition: This creates an information bottleneck: the hidden state has finite capacity, while the sequence may contain many distinct facts, references, and relationships.

query.definition: It encodes search criteria in a learned vector space.

key.definition: Whereas the query represents what the current position is looking for, the key represents what a position makes available for matching.

value.definition: The value is the content that position contributes if attention selects it.

attention_score.definition: The query–key comparison becomes an attention score through a dot product.

scaled_attention_score.definition: The dot product must be scaled before it is used.

claims.text: A recurrent network processes a sequence one token at a time and updates a single hidden state after reading each token.
tags: Attention provides direct access to the input sequence rather than requiring all relevant information to survive in one running hidden state.
A query vector represents what a token position needs to find.
A key vector represents what a position makes available for matching.
A value vector carries the content a position contributes when selected.
Queries, keys, and values are produced by separate learned linear projections.
Attention compares each query with every available key using a dot product.
Dot-product attention scores are scaled by the square root of the key dimension.
Scaled scores express relative compatibility but are not yet attention weights or combined values.

SupportBot.current_state: For the phrase “that charge,” the position's query represents a need related to resolving which earlier transaction is referenced. It is compared with keys from earlier words and the rest of the message; a transaction description may receive a high score and unrelated details lower scores. The scores remain unnormalized compatibility values, and no value has yet been combined into the representation.

sec_01_01.abstract: This section taught how attention separates information seeking, matching, and retrieval into query, key, and value vectors. It explained that queries represent what a position needs, keys represent what positions offer for matching, and values carry the content contributed after selection. It showed how learned projections produce these vectors, how query–key dot products create compatibility scores, and why scores are scaled by the square root of the key dimension. It ended before score normalization and value aggregation.
